articles.title: Alcaraz puts Zverev in shade as world’s best beats No 1 for first ATP Finals title
articles.summary: Spaniard wins final 6-2, 7-6 (7) against new world No 1. Alcaraz the fourth to win career grand slam and ATP Finals. The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names.
body: So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year.

After starting 2026 by becoming the youngest man in history to earn the career grand slam, he is now, at 23, the fourth man to win all four grand slams and the ATP Finals. Despite his long absence, he has missed only two of the four majors and two of the nine Masters 1000 events: the Canadian Open and Shanghai Masters.

Faster indoor courts were previously viewed as the conditions that make Alcaraz most vulnerable. It is fair to say that this is no longer true. Alcaraz ends his year on a 14-match winning streak after triumphing on two of the fastest courts, Paris and Turin.

articles.title: European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal
articles.summary: Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty. Juventus put four past Venezia, Paris FC climb to second. Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.
body: Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou, and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

“We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barcelona midfielder Pedri told Dazn. “Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.”

articles.title: Price wins Grand Slam to end major title wait
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price ends his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powers to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final.
body: The Welshman last won a major title when he claimed the World Series in 2022, but finally got over the line after defeats in three finals in 2026.

The 41-year-old was the runner-up at the World Matchplay, World Grand Prix and World Series, as well as suffering semi-final exits in the Premier League, World Masters, UK Open and European Championships.
This title has been long overdue and Price won it in spectacular fashion with a mid-match burst.
Despite six breaks of throw in the opening 14 legs - including brilliant 150 and 145 checkouts from Price - the game was level at 7-7.

articles.title: Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red
articles.summary: Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at ­Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for ­denying…
body: Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liver­pool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s history.

“Poch is at the wheel” was the mocking, merciless soundtrack that accompanied the end of the former Tottenham, Chelsea and USA coach’s first traumatic game in the job. There may well be more. On this evidence, 19th in the Premier League is not a misleading reflection of United’s position.

The latest calamity in United’s worst start to a season for 40 years cannot be pinned on a head coach who met his new charges only on Wednesday. There can be no genuine takes on Pochettino’s vision for United either, given how quickly he was forced to turn his first game into a damage-limitation exercise. But there was one firm conclusion to be drawn. His first big call in the job proved a serious mistake with destructive repercussions for United’s entire evening.

articles.title: McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton
articles.summary: Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.
body: Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.

A blisteringly cold November afternoon in Hull, against a promoted side where the expectation for a team challenging for the title is to win, and perhaps win with minimum fuss, too. On another afternoon, Brighton may have done just that, were it not for the heroics of Hull’s goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis.

But the best teams, the ones that end the seasons lifting the silverware, almost always seem to find a way. Tzolakis was the Seagulls’ scourge with a string of sensational saves that kept Hull in a contest where, for large periods, they were struggling to keep their heads above water.

articles.title: Thitikul completes three-peat at LPGA Tour finale and breaks money record
articles.summary: Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida.
body: Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.
She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Thitikul becomes the first player to win an LPGA Tour event three years running since Inbee Park at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship from 2013-2015, with her latest a fifth of another memorable season.
A $4m (£3.06m) first prize also sees her end Annika Sorenstam's 25-year stint at the top of the LPGA Tour's career money list, moving ahead of the Swede with a total of $24,292,858 (£20.3m).

articles.title: Gary Neville on De Ligt selection and 'negligent' Man Utd
articles.summary: Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their back line as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.
body: Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.
United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.
"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."

Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.

articles.title: Billie Jean King Hopes to ‘Help Any Gay Kid or Trans Kid’ and ‘Affect the Future Generations’ with New Doc (Exclusive)
articles.summary: NEED TO KNOW. Billie Jean King’s new documentary features candid interviews and unseen footage of the tennis champion and aims to inspire younger generations to make a difference in the world. King has spent her life and career advocating for women and the LGBTQ+ community.
body: When Billie Jean King was 12 years old, she had an “epiphany.” The former world No. 1 tennis player tells PEOPLE: “I wanted to make the world a better place.
Now, 71 years and 39 Grand Slam titles later, King, 83, a pioneer for gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights in sports, continues to honor that promise with her new documentary Give Me the Ball!.

Featuring candid interviews and never-before-seen footage, the film, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January and is now streaming on ESPN, offers an intimate look at how the tennis champion risked her career, relationships and public standing to fight for equality on and off the court.

“I think that if I hadn’t played tennis, I definitely would’ve gone to law school, gotten into politics because I think it’s really important to lead if you can,” King explains. “You never know how [documentaries] are going to affect another human being, but I wanted this to be real.”
